title: Money-path coverage map: none of the 39 registered money-path S0/S1 findings would be caught on the real path by any integration or fork test; the real-path fork tests that exist prove buy landing, sell recording and the failed-held resume SQL, but every registered defect sits on a branch they mock, stub, skip or never drive

evidence.ref: node over .planning/audit/findings/*.json (register read, no src import): every finding with severity S0 or S1, excluding the RAIL and TESTU test-infrastructure items
evidence.note: 39 money-path items: AUD-BUY-001 (S0) and 38 S1s across BUY, EXIT, ANTIRUG, TX, DB and API
real path proven: the real V2 handler buys, the engine's own poll loop fires the stop-loss, the sell row carries a decoded amount_out
real path proven: V2 and V3 handlers buy real tokens on a fork and some exit sells (path unasserted, AUD-TESTI-019)
real path proven: the production resume statements find an exit_failed_held row (the S-1 fix)
real path proven in-process only: executeDeliberateBuy lands and arms inside the test worker

sibling_sites_checked: All 27 integration and 23 fork files of the slice, read in full at the base SHA (fork files not executed), against the evidence of every registered S0/S1 money-path finding read from the register (findings JSON only, no SUMMARY or VERIFICATION doc). Unit tests are TESTU scope (22-23).
severity_rationale: S2 by the rubric (test/infra drift that hides S0/S1); the S0 and S1s themselves are already registered and escalated in their own slices. The point of this entry is the map Phase 23 needs: zero of 39 are caught on the real path, five are encoded as expected behaviour, three sit on fork paths that run but do not assert them.
recommendation: Phase 23 (real-path triage): use this map as the work list; for each item build a RED real-path reproduction (fork or scripted-provider harness) before any fix. Phase 25 owns the first fork execution; Phase 28 rewrites the tests named in the sub-claims.
escaped_regression: Every registered item listed in the sub-claims is a regression that is live today with the integration and fork suites green; for example AUD-BUY-001: a deliberate buy run from scripts/deliberate-buy.ts lands and is left with no exit monitor and no anti-rug protection while deliberateBuyReplay passes.

sub_claims.claim: AUD-BUY-001 (S0, deliberate buy armed only inside the short-lived script): deliberateBuyReplay asserts the monitor and anti-rug registration exist right after executeDeliberateBuy returns, inside the long-lived Vitest worker; the production caller scripts/deliberate-buy.ts exits after the buy and no test runs it. The fork test passes on exactly the in-process arming the S0 says dies with the script.
sub_claims.status: not caught (a test pins the defect as expected behaviour)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-BUY-002 (landed buy treated as a clean failure): no integration or fork case throws after submission; killswitch, v2/v3HoneypotIntegration mock sendTxWithRetry and the fork handlers land cleanly.
AUD-BUY-003 (snipe minOut 0 when the quote fails): no test fails the pre-buy quote; integration mocks return fixed getAmountsOut, fork buys quote successfully.
AUD-BUY-004 (double-buy race): no test runs two handlers for one token concurrently.
AUD-BUY-005 (no unhandledRejection handler): no test lets a rejection escape or checks that the process survives one.
AUD-BUY-006 (Telegram allowlist allow-all): no integration or fork test runs the Telegram listener.
evidence: git grep -n telegramListener 23a64617dca167976adc4645fed0e2c69e384820 -- test/integration test/fork (mock factories only)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-BUY-008 (DEX WebSocket reconnect): the reconnect cases compute backoff in the test (AUD-TESTI-013); no DEX reconnect runs.
AUD-BUY-010 (risk limits checked early, concurrent overspend): canSnipe is mocked in every integration buy test; the fork replays set permissive caps and run one buy at a time.
AUD-BUY-011 (stop chain does not stop buying): the stop case asserts the stopped set only (AUD-TESTI-008).
AUD-BUY-025 (deliberate public buy wait with no timeout in the nonce lock): the fork deliberate buy uses passthrough with interval mining, so wait(3) always settles; a never-mined tx is not modelled.
AUD-DB-001 (malformed risk settings disable the limits): the fork sets numeric caps; no test sets a non-numeric risk env.

AUD-DB-002 (daily-loss and exposure compare decimal and wei): realLaunchReplay writes real decimal buy rows and wei sell rows for three fixtures into one temp DB, so the corrupted exposure and loss values exist, but the caps are 1000 / 99% and no test reads getTotalExposure or getDailyRealizedLoss after a sell.
sub_claims.status: not caught (path runs, defect not asserted)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-DB-003 (failed-held positions excluded from the risk queries): exitStatePersistence Test 3 builds a failed-held position (trades.status failed) but asserts only the resume, never the risk queries.
sub_claims.status: not caught (path runs, defect not asserted)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-DB-004 (no DB row until the whole submission returns): no test interrupts between submit and the row write.
AUD-DB-007 (DB path resolves against cwd, empty DB created): every DB-using test sets an absolute temp DB_PATH.
AUD-EXIT-001 (private sells accept any output): the fork uses passthrough (no private path) and integration sells are mocked.
AUD-EXIT-002 (monitor never starts when the first quote fails): no test fails the first post-buy quote; the integration case passes {} and asserts null only (AUD-TESTI-010).
AUD-EXIT-003 (the exit signal is not a price): the fork exits fire on pumps and dumps large enough that any ratio signal trips; no test asserts the quoted price.
sub_claims.status: not caught (path runs, defect not asserted)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-EXIT-007 (exits that return false not marked failed-held): no test makes an exit return false.
AUD-EXIT-008 (dashboard sells sent as routine exits): controls.test pins urgency-market-sell (AUD-TESTI-007).
sub_claims.status: not caught (a test pins the defect as expected behaviour)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-EXIT-009 (exit wait() with no timeout in the nonce lock): fork sells use passthrough with interval mining, so the wait settles.

AUD-EXIT-013 (positions resumed or sold through the first dex of their type): every fork position is on uniswap-v2 / uniswap-v3 (the first dex of each type) and exitStatePersistence re-implements the first-dex lookup (AUD-TESTI-026).
sub_claims.status: not caught (a test pins the defect as expected behaviour)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-EXIT-014 (anti-rug exit refused behind the sell lock): the anti-rug tests mock executeFullSell and exitManager.

AUD-EXIT-015 (probe size not stored, resume uses the current snipe amount): the fork resumes pass "0.05" or ctx.chain.snipeAmount, equal to the buy amount, so the mismatch never arises; exitStatePersistence Test 3 passes ctx.chain.snipeAmount as production does.
sub_claims.status: not caught (a test pins the defect as expected behaviour)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-ANTIRUG-001 (three reconnect paths rewrite ctx.wsProvider): no test combines the anti-rug, DEX and dashboard reconnect paths on a real provider.
AUD-ANTIRUG-002 (refused reconnect kills the bot): reconnect failure is modelled as a constructor throw (AUD-TESTI-004).
AUD-ANTIRUG-003 (breaker counts dispatches, not rugs): every anti-rug test feeds one log per position (multiSignalEnd2End, antiRugDetector.fork).
AUD-ANTIRUG-004 (refused escape never retried): executeFullSell is mocked to resolve true in every anti-rug test.
AUD-ANTIRUG-005 (backfill fires live exits): the backfill no-exit case swaps the evaluator for a double (AUD-TESTI-004).
AUD-ANTIRUG-011 (re-registered with the first dex of its type): single-dex fixtures and an unasserted dex argument (AUD-TESTI-006); the fork resume re-implements the same lookup (AUD-TESTI-026).
sub_claims.status: not caught (a test pins the defect as expected behaviour)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-API-001 (emergency/force sell skip still-held failed positions): the position SQL is stubbed (AUD-TESTI-007).
AUD-API-002 (stop chain removes the anti-rug subscription): the stop case requires removeAllListeners (AUD-TESTI-008).
sub_claims.status: not caught (a test pins the defect as expected behaviour)

sub_claims.claim: AUD-API-008 (malformed Host on an upgrade kills the process): wsPush mocks the upgrade handler; no test sends an Upgrade request.
AUD-TX-001 (non-reentrant nonce lock): no integration test takes withNonceLock re-entrantly; the fork runs the real lock one operation at a time.
AUD-TX-002 (never-settling wait inside the nonce lock): the passthrough timeout case fakes a rejection ethers cannot produce (AUD-TESTI-003); the fork uses interval mining.
AUD-TX-003 (head-of-line blocking through private attempts): the fork has no relay (passthrough) and integration mocks the strategy.
AUD-TX-004 (duplicate module instance): no test loads the nonce authority twice.
AUD-TX-005 (no single-instance process lock): no test starts two bot processes.
AUD-TX-009 (Flashbots bundle wait RPC hiccup crashes the bot): the Flashbots library is mocked in integration and the fork has no relay.
